dataset_capability_audit_summary.location: G:\MDPI Symmetry\data\CRAG\OpenDataLab___CRAG\raw\CRAG\extracted\CRAG (user-provided, downloaded from OpenDataLab after the official Warwick source proved inaccessible without institutional SSO)
dataset_capability_audit_summary.provenance: Colorectal Adenocarcinoma Gland (CRAG) Dataset v2, released with the MILD-Net paper (Graham et al., Medical Image Analysis 2019); acquired from University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, curated by the University of Warwick Tissue Image Analytics (TIA) lab.
dataset_capability_audit_summary.image_dimensions: 8 distinct sizes, all approx 1500-1514 (W) x 1516 (H); no resizing needed, all >> 128px patch size
dataset_capability_audit_summary.image_format: PNG, RGB, no corruption detected (PIL verify() on all 213), no exact-duplicate files (content MD5, all 213 unique)
dataset_capability_audit_summary.annotation_format: PNG, uint8, single-channel, instance-labeled (0=background, 1..N=gland instance id) -- STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to GlaS's mask format
dataset_capability_audit_summary.annotation_pairing: all 213 images have exactly one matching Annotation file by filename stem; zero unpaired files
dataset_capability_audit_summary.pathology_labels: NONE FOUND. No CSV/JSON/XML/grade file of any kind exists anywhere in the archive beyond README.txt. CRAG provides images + instance masks + human-readable overlays ONLY -- no benign/malignant, no tumor grade, no clinical metadata of any kind.
dataset_capability_audit_summary.patient_metadata: NONE FOUND -- no patient/case identifiers anywhere in the distribution.
dataset_capability_audit_summary.official_splits: train/ (173 images) and valid/ (40 images, files prefixed 'test_') -- README calls the 40-image folder the 'test set'; the folder is literally named 'valid'. This is CRAG's OWN split for people training on CRAG; Model 3 was never trained on ANY CRAG image (train or valid), so both are equally 'held out' from Model 3's perspective -- see population definition below.
dataset_capability_audit_summary.license: README.txt states only a citation requirement (must cite the MILD-Net paper); no separate machine-readable LICENSE file was found in the archive.

gland_instance_stats.note: using the EXACT unmodified Stage 4 thresholds (MIN_GLAND_PIXELS=20, BORDER_FRAC_THRESHOLD=0.02, DEFAULT_S_THRESHOLD=0.15) -- none were changed or tuned for CRAG.

dataset_capability_audit_summary.compatibility_finding_CRITICAL: 70 of 213 images (33%) contain at least one gland instance whose area exceeds 30% of that image's total pixel area (30 instances exceed 50%; the single largest instance covers 92.9% of its image). All such large instances are single connected components (n_connected_components=1), not an artifact of the fragmentation check. GlaS's largest gland instance, by contrast, is 358,105 px (well under any comparable image-area fraction). This indicates CRAG's annotation convention frequently labels large, fused/cribriform glandular regions -- common in more aggressive colorectal adenocarcinoma histology -- as a SINGLE gland instance, whereas GlaS's instances are, on average, much smaller and more numerous relative to image size. This is a genuine, documented ANNOTATION-CONVENTION DIFFERENCE, not a data defect and not something corrected here: the existing Stage 4 validity rules (which check only too-small, border-truncation, numerical instability, and near-isotropy) do not flag these large fused instances, and per instruction section 15 ('do not tune validity thresholds on CRAG'), no new upper-size exclusion rule is introduced. These large instances are therefore treated as VALID under the unchanged GlaS rule set and will contribute to the CRAG anatomical target -- but their PCA-derived orientation represents a much coarser, less spatially localized quantity than a typical GlaS gland's orientation, which materially limits how directly 'gland-level anatomical correspondence' can be compared between the two datasets. This limitation is carried into the final interpretation, not hidden.

external_independence_assessment.same_institution_and_group: CONFIRMED: both GlaS and CRAG were acquired from the same source hospital (University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire, UHCW) and curated by the same research group (Warwick TIA lab) -- verified via the MILD-Net paper and Warwick's own dataset pages. Independence is therefore NOT claimed in the strong sense of 'unrelated cohort/institution/scanner pipeline'.
external_independence_assessment.exact_duplicate_check: EXHAUSTIVE: all 165 GlaS images vs all 213 CRAG images compared by content MD5 hash -- zero exact matches.
external_independence_assessment.near_duplicate_check: PARTIAL/SAMPLED ONLY: a 20x20 grayscale-thumbnail L2-distance comparison on a small sample from each dataset found no near-identical images; this is NOT an exhaustive 165x213 near-duplicate search and is reported as a limited, sampled check, not proof of zero near-duplicates.
external_independence_assessment.conclusion: CRAG is a DISTINCT, non-overlapping image set from GlaS (no shared files, no shared patient/case identifiers available to check further), but it is NOT institutionally or cohort-independent in the strong sense -- both datasets share source hospital and curating lab. This stage therefore uses the term 'external cross-dataset validation' throughout and explicitly avoids the terms 'independent proof' or 'definitive replication', per instruction section 11.

frozen_model.loading: model.eval() then load_state_dict(), torch.no_grad() for all inference; no optimizer, no gradient step, no checkpoint selection -- identical loading pattern to Stages 11/12/16.

target_construction.method: IDENTICAL, UNMODIFIED Stage 4 pipeline: anatomy_targets.py::analyze_glands (PCA covariance orientation, S_cov/phi_cov) + build_full_image_field (S_choice='cov', DEFAULT_S_THRESHOLD=0.15, exclude_border_truncated=True) -- same thresholds, same coordinate convention, same head-tail symmetry, same Q=[[q1,q2],[q2,-q1]] convention as GlaS. No CRAG-specific tensor definition, eigenvector convention, normalization, or threshold is introduced.
target_construction.validated_compatible: CONFIRMED by direct execution on sample CRAG masks before any design commitment: analyze_glands runs cleanly (0 numerically-unstable instances across all 3054), confirming CRAG's instance-labeled mask format is compatible with the existing mathematical definition without modification.
target_construction.large_fused_instances: Not excluded, not specially handled -- see compatibility_finding_CRITICAL above. Documented as a limitation, not silently repaired.

patch_extraction.rule: IDENTICAL to the established project framework (code/data_prep.py::extract_patches + anatomy_targets.py::crop_field_to_patches) -- unchanged because CRAG's image dimensions (>=1319x1516) comfortably support this patch size without modification.
patch_extraction.rule_source: IDENTICAL, unmodified value from code_v2/phase2_calibration.py::MIN_VALID_FRACTION_FOR_PATCH -- not retuned for CRAG.
patch_extraction.estimated_valid_patches: ~25,000-26,000 across all 213 images (estimated from a 40-image pre-check before full extraction) -- roughly 12x GlaS's pooled testA+testB patch count (2083), because CRAG's tiles are larger and its patch grid therefore denser per image.

population_and_unit_of_analysis.primary_population: ALL 213 CRAG images (173 'train' + 40 'valid'/test) -- Model 3 was never trained on ANY CRAG image, so both of CRAG's own internal splits are equally held-out from Model 3's perspective. Reported separately (CRAG-train, CRAG-test) AND pooled (all 213), mirroring GlaS's testA/testB/pooled convention. No CRAG image is excluded for any reason.
population_and_unit_of_analysis.image_level_primary_unit: Per instruction sections 12-13, IMAGE is treated as the primary independent unit for statistical inference: one (S_DL, phi_DL) and one (S_anat, phi_anat) value per image, each the unweighted mean (in vector (q1,q2) space, then S/phi derived) over that image's valid patches. This is a NEW, but pre-specified-before-results, aggregation rule -- chosen specifically because CRAG's much higher patch density per image (~120 valid patches/image vs GlaS's ~26) would otherwise pseudo-replicate a single image's signal far more than in Stage 11's GlaS analysis.
population_and_unit_of_analysis.patch_level_secondary_diagnostic: For direct comparability with Stage 11's own patch-level metric definition, a SECOND, patch-level analysis is also run using the EXACT SAME compute_full_metrics function as Stage 11, on a deterministic, fixed-seed (42) random subsample of AT MOST 5000 valid patches (stratified proportionally by image), decided now purely for O(n^2) pairwise-permutation memory/compute tractability (Stage 11's own null-construction is O(n^2) in patch count; ~25,000 patches would require an infeasible amount of memory for the exact same procedure). If total valid patches are <=5000 (not expected, but possible if the extraction differs from the pre-check estimate), no subsampling occurs. This subsampling is a computational-tractability decision made before any Model 3 prediction is inspected, not a favorable-result selection.
population_and_unit_of_analysis.gland_level: Not used as a modeling unit (Model 3 predicts per-patch/per-pixel, not per-gland-instance); gland-level statistics are reported only in the dataset/target audit (counts, validity, area).

primary_external_validation.metrics: IDENTICAL formulas to Stage 11's compute_full_metrics: angular correspondence with Glass's Delta, order-magnitude Pearson/Spearman r with bootstrap 95% CI, tensor similarity D_Q with permutation p -- reused unmodified.
primary_external_validation.threshold_policy: The GlaS preregistered numerical thresholds (Glass's Delta>=0.5, r>=0.30, etc.) are REPORTED for descriptive comparison only and are explicitly NOT treated as formal CRAG pass/fail criteria -- the original protocol never established them as external-validation thresholds. No new 'CRAG success threshold' is defined anywhere in this matrix or invented after seeing results.
primary_external_validation.terminology: Results are described as 'external cross-dataset validation', never as 'independent proof' or 'definitive replication', per the independence assessment above.

rotation_consistency.justification_for_inclusion_decided_now: Rotation consistency reuses Stage 12's existing, cheap, no-retraining protocol and directly extends this stage's 'does the frozen representation behave the same way on unseen data' question; included in the frozen scope from the start, not added after seeing anatomical results.
rotation_consistency.population: The same deterministic <=5000-patch subsample used for the patch-level anatomical diagnostic (for direct comparability and shared compute).
rotation_consistency.protocol: IDENTICAL to Stage 12: angle grid [0,15,30,37,45,60,90,123,150,173], skimage.transform.rotate with angle=+alpha_deg, mode='reflect', order=1 (model's own sign convention, unchanged), same normalized_equivariance_error formula, same frozen per-angle local_thresholds from preregistered_thresholds_v2.json.
rotation_consistency.reduction: Center-pixel of the dense (H2,W2) field -- IDENTICAL to Stage 12's original definition (not Stage 16's multi-scale sweep; multi-scale is explicitly NOT included in this stage, see below), for maximum direct comparability with the ORIGINAL Stage 12 result.
rotation_consistency.threshold_policy: Pass/fail is reported ONLY as a descriptive comparison against the ORIGINAL frozen Stage 12 threshold (>=7/9 non-zero angles) -- this is explicitly NOT a new official Criterion D decision for CRAG.

multiscale_analysis.reason_decided_now: To control scope and compute, and because Stage 16 already established the frozen 6-scale set exists for a SEPARATE diagnostic purpose on GlaS, multi-scale evaluation is not included in this stage's frozen design. Per instruction section 17, it is not added after seeing primary CRAG results; a dedicated future stage with its own design freeze would be required to extend Stage 16's scale sweep to CRAG.

planned_comparisons: image dimensions (GlaS ~775x522 vs CRAG ~1500-1516 square-ish tiles)
gland area distribution (GlaS mean 21,363px vs CRAG mean 74,425px)
fraction of images with a dominant (>30% area) fused gland instance (GlaS: not previously characterized this way; CRAG: 33%, computed above)
domain_shift_descriptive_variables.purpose: descriptive characterization only -- explicitly not used to explain away, excuse, or retroactively justify any CRAG correspondence result in either direction, per instruction section 18.

statistical_inference.unit_for_bootstrap: IMAGE for the image-level primary analysis (resampling images with replacement); patches within the patch-level secondary diagnostic follow Stage 11's own established patch-level bootstrap convention unchanged, for direct comparability with that specific prior result.
statistical_inference.no_cross_dataset_pooling: GlaS and CRAG results are NEVER pooled into a single combined statistic anywhere in this stage -- always reported side by side, descriptively.

no_test_set_rescue_restated: All 213 CRAG images are used; none are excluded as 'difficult'.

The <=5000-patch subsample for the patch-level/rotation analyses is a PRE-SPECIFIED, fixed-seed, tractability-driven sampling rule decided before any Model 3 output on CRAG exists -- it is not a favorable-subset selection and does not affect the image-level primary analysis, which uses all 213 images.
